Use case: identity-preserve. Create a production 2D illustrated RPG WALK sprite sheet for ONLY the silver-haired female expedition captain in the FIRST ROW of input image 1. Image 1 is the exact approved character and painted/pixel illustration style: tan skin, long silver hair, teal scarf and cape with gold trim, navy flight armor, ivory forearm/knee plates, gold belt and navy boots. Preserve that design and its sophisticated illustrated detail. Do not depict the other three characters. Input image 2 is ONLY an example of sprite-sheet organization and distinct frame-by-frame animation, not the character design or art style.

Output: exactly 8 equal columns by 4 equal rows, 32 full-body sprites. Landscape 2048 by 1280 if possible. Each cell has the same generous transparent margins and ground anchor. Absolutely no text, labels, grid lines, cast shadows or scenery. Genuine transparent PNG background with an alpha channel; NEVER paint a checkerboard into the image.

Row 1: captain walking toward the viewer (front).
Row 2: captain walking away (back).
Row 3: captain walking toward screen left.
Row 4: captain walking toward screen right.
All 8 columns in EACH row are consecutive poses of ONE looping WALK, not direction changes: left heel contact, left down, left stance/right passing, left up, right heel contact, right down, right stance/left passing, right up. Legs alternate convincingly; stance foot is grounded, swing foot bends at the knee. Arms counter-swing with opposite leg. Hair and cape follow with subtle overlapping motion. Keep head/body size, costume details, color and perspective identical across all cells. Boots are clearly separated and anatomically attached. Modest natural walk, no running, jumping or lunging, no puppet distortion. Final column flows naturally back to first. Each sprite centered on the exact same cell anchor and occupies about 80 percent of cell height; no sprite touches a cell boundary. Entire sheet is illustrated 2D game art matching image 1, NEVER plastic 3D models.
side_cycle:
Create an eight-frame illustrated pixel-RPG walk animation of the silver-haired space captain from the FIRST ROW of the reference. Preserve her exact navy armor, gold belt, ivory knee/forearm plates, teal cape, long silver hair, tan skin and high-detail drawn sprite style. ONLY this one character. No 3D render.

Exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows, read left to right, top to bottom. ALL eight sprites face SCREEN RIGHT, exact side profile, same scale and anchored pelvis. This is ONE complete animated walk, with DRAMATICALLY DISTINCT leg silhouettes:
1 LEFT CONTACT: left boot far forward touching ground, right boot far behind touching ground, legs form wide inverted V; right arm forward.
2 LEFT DOWN: forward left knee bent accepting weight; right rear heel lifting; body slightly lower.
3 LEFT PASSING: weight on straight left leg directly under hip, RIGHT knee raised and folded forward, feet near each other rather than split.
4 LEFT UP: left heel raised under body; RIGHT thigh advancing with knee bent; right arm back.
5 RIGHT CONTACT: right boot far forward touching ground, left boot far behind, opposite arm swing from frame 1.
6 RIGHT DOWN: forward right knee bent bearing weight, left heel lifting.
7 RIGHT PASSING: weight on straight right leg under hip, LEFT knee raised and folded, feet near each other.
8 RIGHT UP: right heel raised; LEFT thigh advances with knee bent, preparing loop into 1.
The feet must visibly alternate between widely separated contact poses and almost-overlapping passing poses. Do NOT repeat the same open-leg pose eight times. In the passing poses, the silhouette has ONE long supporting leg and ONE folded raised leg. Keep the torso, head and costume consistent. Subtle cape overlap, no floating, no running.

Each of 8 cells has an equal canvas, same foot ground line, plenty of blank border. Exact 4-by-2 arrangement. No text, no cell labels, no grid lines, no cast shadows. GENUINELY TRANSPARENT PNG with alpha, NOT a picture of a transparency checkerboard. Never draw checkerboard squares. Clean crisp cutout contours. Draw this as a functional animation sheet, not a lineup of cosmetic costume variations.
